lens: Statistics and study design, judged from the manuscript text and its artifact (research/manuscripts/fusion-partner/emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json) at the pin: does each interval mean what the sentence uses it for; are the pooled cohorts independent and the denominator convention consistent; is a pooled figure a cancellation of two disagreeing cohorts; post-hoc testing and multiplicity; the direction of the uncensored during-follow-up bias; what the record establishes about adjustment versus what the paper claims; and any sentence claiming a magnitude, a prediction or an independence where the record supports only a direction. Every printed Wilson bound and every printed Fisher p was independently recomputed from the artifact's integer counts.
verdict: REVISE — 3 blockers, 4 P1s, 6 P2s. The arithmetic is clean: all 22 Wilson bounds and all 5 Fisher p-values recompute exactly, every denominator reconciles across the three analyses, the zero-event arm is handled correctly, post-hoc status and non-correction for multiplicity are declared, and the paper's central self-limiting claims (direction not magnitude; crude not adjusted; the interval cannot exclude equality) are stated at their true weight. What fails is three COMPARATIVE claims built on top of correct numbers: a retracted two-series adjustment claim that survived in §3.8, a falsification threshold in §6 that the arithmetic contradicts, and a bias-direction argument that is circular for the one endpoint that carries the headline. None of the three is watched by the prose-vs-artifact guard, because that guard binds values and never the relation a sentence asserts between them.
central_claim: That the NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a candidate (not established) stratification variable in EMC: a crude pooled disease-specific-death contrast of 7/15 = 46.7 % (24.8–69.9) TAF15 vs 6/58 = 10.3 % (4.8–20.8) EWSR1 over two cohorts and 73 patients, defeated in its own larger cohort by a multivariable model in which the partner loses significance to tumour size; and a treatment-response signal that is a direction only — 0 of 3–5 TAF15 patients, 95 % Wilson upper bound 43.4–56.1 %, above the comparator arm's point estimate in both analyses.

blockers.where: §3.8, final paragraph ('An attribution correction: whose hedge, and when')
blockers.quote: Three later observations are consistent with reading the partner as a **surrogate for something downstream** rather than as a mechanism, and all three are above: the prognostic effect is absorbed by tumour size in the two largest series (§3.4), Paioli 2021 cannot reach significance on it at all (§3.4), and the matched ex vivo pair shows partner-independent drug response for the one class it tested (§3.7).
blockers.why_wrong: 'Absorbed by tumour size in the two largest series' asserts an ADJUSTMENT RESULT for two cohorts when the record establishes it for one. The two largest partner-stratified series in this synthesis are Paioli 2021 (n=67, §4.1 calls 67 the largest anywhere here) and Huang 2023 (n=58), so the sentence necessarily includes Paioli — yet §3.4 states in terms that Paioli's adjustment structure 'is not stated in any record held here', is 'UNKNOWN rather than established', and 'is not counted as a second multivariable result'. This is the exact claim Appendix A17 retracts ('Two series … tested the partner as a prognostic factor in a multivariable model. Neither found it independent.' and 'both series that adjusted lost the partner to tumour size'), surviving at a third site the correction did not reach — the one-of-a-pair class. It is also internally incoherent: the next clause in the same sentence lists Paioli separately as observation two, so observation one either double-counts Paioli or names a second adjusted series that does not exist. A reader takes away that the size confound is replicated in two independent adjusted analyses; the record has one (Huang), an UNKNOWN (Paioli), and no replication.
blockers.evidence: Document §3.4: 'For Paioli 2021 this repository holds only what its abstract reports: the partner reaches no conventional significance while size does, in an analysis whose adjustment structure **is not stated in any record held here**. Its full text is closed (§6), so whether that contrast was adjusted is UNKNOWN rather than established, and it is not counted as a second multivariable result.' | Document Appendix A17 registers the retracted form. | Artifact cohorts[paioli-2021-outcome].published_p_values.note: 'Whether this analysis was adjusted is NOT recorded in anything held here, so it is not counted as a second multivariable result.' | Artifact carries multivariable_result on huang-2023-outcome ONLY (grep: one occurrence). | §4.1: 'The largest partner-stratified series anywhere in this synthesis has 67 patients' (= Paioli).

blockers.where: §6, falsifier #5 — and the same sentence in the artifact, what_could_kill_this[4]
blockers.quote: A **third** outcome cohort with per-partner event counts in which TAF15 mortality is not elevated. The pooled crude death contrast rests on two TAF15 arms of 7 and 8 patients; a third of similar size disagreeing would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval.
blockers.why_wrong: The stated falsification threshold is arithmetically false under every reading, and it understates the result's robustness by a large factor. The pooled TAF15 numerator is 7 deaths in 15. Adding a third cohort of 'similar size' (7–8 TAF15 patients) with mortality 'not elevated' gives: 0/8 -> 7/23 = 30.4 %; 0/7 -> 7/22 = 31.8 %; 1/8 (i.e. matching the EWSR1 rate) -> 8/23 = 34.8 %; 1/7 -> 8/22 = 36.4 %. The comparator arm's Wilson interval is 4.8–20.8 %, so none of these lands inside it, and the gap is not marginal. Recomputing the comparator interval after that third cohort also contributes an EWSR1 arm makes it worse, not better: adding 5/42 gives 11/100, Wilson 6.3–18.6 %, and adding 4/40 gives 10/98, Wilson 5.6–17.8 %. To bring 7/n to <= 20.8 % requires n >= 34, i.e. about NINETEEN further TAF15 patients with zero additional deaths — two to three more cohorts, not 'a third of similar size'. A reader calibrating the fragility of the headline from this bullet is misled about how much new data would overturn it, and the falsifier as written cannot be executed as stated.
blockers.evidence: Artifact analyses.B_outcome_by_partner.disease_specific_death.taf15_arm = {events:7, denom:15}; comparator_arm = {events:6, denom:58, ci95_lo_percent:4.8, ci95_hi_percent:20.8}. Recomputed Wilson (z=1.959964) reproduces 4.8–20.8 exactly. Pooled TAF15 point estimates after a third cohort: 7/22=31.8 %, 7/23=30.4 %, 8/22=36.4 %, 8/23=34.8 % — all above every comparator upper bound tested (20.8, 18.6, 17.8, 19.0). 7/0.208 = 33.65, so n>=34. Identical claim carried in artifact what_could_kill_this[4], so this is a defect in both files rather than prose drift from the artifact.

blockers.where: §3.3, second estimand caveat (and its stronger form in the artifact's cohort record)
blockers.quote: Second, **follow-up is unequal and, in one cohort, unstated**: Agaram's arms differ about two-fold in mean follow-up (21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing *against* the TAF15 arm accruing events) and Huang publishes no per-arm follow-up at all.
blockers.why_wrong: The bias direction is asserted as established for a table whose headline row is disease-specific death, and for that row it is circular. These are uncensored during-follow-up proportions: follow-up ENDS AT DEATH, so a cohort arm in which 3 of 7 patients died of disease has its mean follow-up shortened BY the very events being counted. The TAF15 arm's 21.7-month mean is therefore at least partly a CONSEQUENCE of the death excess, not an independent handicap the excess overcame — so the imbalance cannot be used to argue the death contrast is conservatively estimated. (For the recurrence and metastasis rows the argument is sound, because survivors accrue observation time; the manuscript applies it to 'the table above', which includes death.) The artifact states the invalid inference outright and the manuscript's caveat is what a reader would carry away from it. Nothing in the design can establish the claimed direction for the death row without a censored (time-to-event) analysis, and §2.5 states no time-to-event quantity is estimated anywhere in this work. The honest form is that the follow-up imbalance is outcome-dependent and its net direction on the death row is UNKNOWN.
blockers.evidence: Artifact cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning: 'The bias runs AGAINST the TAF15 arm accruing events, so the death excess is observed despite shorter observation, while the recurrence comparison is confounded in the direction that produced this cohort's metastasis reversal.' | Same cohort record: strata['TAF15::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 21.7 with disease_specific_death {events:3, denom:7}; strata['EWSR1::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 43.3 with disease_specific_death {events:1, denom:16}. | Document §2.4/§2.5: 'No time-to-event quantity is estimated anywhere in this work.' | Document §4.7 restates the same pair with no direction attached, so §3.3 is the only site making the claim.

p1s.quote: **I².** Not computed, for the same reason. The honest heterogeneity signal at this scale is the **range of per-cohort rates**, printed beside every pooled figure — §3.1 for the TKI-response secondary pool, §3.3 for each of the three outcome rows, §3.5 for prevalence — and computed in the artifact's `heterogeneity` blocks
p1s.why_wrong: 'The same reason' points at the preceding bullet, whose justification is explicitly scoped: 'Across the TKI-response and outcome-by-partner strata (§3.1, §3.3) the per-stratum denominator runs from three … to fifty-eight … and the event count from zero … to fourteen; a between-study variance is not estimable at that scale.' That reasoning does not cover §3.5, which is four cohorts, n = 154, 28 TAF15 events, per-cohort denominators 24/57/11/62 and a per-cohort spread of 13.4 points — a scale at which Cochran's Q and I-squared are computable and would be informative. The paper's own list then extends the no-heterogeneity-modelling decision to §3.5 anyway, and the artifact reuses the identical boilerplate note verbatim there ('at these stratum sizes a between-study variance estimate would be uninterpretable'), where it is a copy rather than an argument. This is P1 rather than a blocker because the prevalence figures themselves are right and §4.2 disclaims meta-analytic guarantees globally — but it is the analysis whose homogeneity-assuming Wilson interval is then used comparatively ('sits below the 29.2 %', Abstract and §5), which is the one place the unmodelled heterogeneity bites. An ordinary future edit adding a fifth prevalence series would inherit the same unexamined justification.
p1s.evidence: Document §2.5, random-effects bullet (scope sentence) and I-squared bullet ('for the same reason'). | Artifact analyses.C_partner_prevalence.heterogeneity_TAF15: per_cohort_percent {agaram 29.2, huang 15.8, lenz 18.2, paioli 16.1}, spread_percent 13.4, method_note identical string to the two-cohort blocks in analyses.B. | analyses.C_partner_prevalence.partner_assigned_per_cohort {24, 57, 11, 62}.

p1s.where: Abstract, §3.1, §3.3, §5 — every place a gap is printed; artifact field `comparator_minus_taf15_percentage_points`
p1s.quote: a 36.3-point gap, post-hoc Fisher p = 0.0034, and the first magnitude this contrast has ever had
p1s.why_wrong: No interval is printed on any DIFFERENCE anywhere in the paper or the artifact. Every comparative magnitude — 36.3, 9.2 and 4.3 points in §3.3, 21.1 and 37.0 points in §3.1 — is a bare point estimate, while the paper's whole claim structure is about differences and it calls 36.3 'the first magnitude this contrast has ever had'. A Newcombe (or Wilson-based) interval on the difference of two proportions is computable from exactly the counts the artifact already holds and is the natural companion to the arm-wise Wilson intervals POLICY §2.2 mandates; its absence forces the reader to reconstruct uncertainty from the two arm intervals, which is the invalid substitute the paper itself then uses (STAT-P2-3). This is P1 rather than a blocker because the gaps are arithmetically correct and §4.2 labels the pooled figures descriptive — but a magnitude offered as the paper's contribution with no stated uncertainty is one edit away from being quoted as an estimate, and nothing in the guard suite would notice.
p1s.evidence: Artifact: `comparator_minus_taf15_percentage_points` is a scalar in all six contrast blocks (analyses.A primary and secondary; analyses.B death, local_recurrence, distant_metastasis_after_presentation; analyses.B.huang_only_metastasis_readings) with no companion interval field; grep of the artifact returns no difference-interval key of any kind. | Document §3.3 table prints a 'gap' column with no interval; §5 claims bullets print 36.3 and 9.2 points with no interval.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py — BINDINGS construction (guard gap, P1 by construction)
p1s.quote:
# ⭐ THE UPPER-BOUND RANGE AND BOTH COMPARATOR POINT ESTIMATES IN ONE CONSTRUCTION, because the
# sentence's whole force is that the bound sits ABOVE both — checking them separately would let a
# repair move one and leave the comparison reading as though it still held.
p1s.why_wrong: The guard binds the VALUES that appear inside a relational sentence but never asserts the RELATION the sentence claims. The comment above shows the author reasoning about exactly this risk and then solving only half of it: the four numbers are read together, so a repair cannot move one in isolation — but nothing asserts `taf15_upper_ci > comparator_percent`. If a future artifact regeneration made the comparator point estimate exceed the TAF15 upper bound, the binding would still match and the sentence 'sits above the comparator arm's point estimate in both analyses' would ship as a false statement. The same hole covers every other comparative sentence in the paper: 'an interval that contains the ≈20 %' (nothing asserts 12.9 <= 20 <= 25.0 — the artifact's own `falls_inside_pooled_interval: true` is a stored boolean, not a recomputed one), 'sits below the 29.2 %', 'the pooled gap is 9.2 points with overlapping intervals', and §6 falsifier #5's 'would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval' — which carries no number at all and is therefore invisible to both numeric censuses, which is exactly why STAT-B2 could stand. The census tests are honest about this ('THIS IS COVERAGE, NOT CORRECTNESS'), but no other test closes it.
p1s.evidence: guard file, bind() for the upper-bound sentence (regex captures four values, lambda returns four artifact values, no inequality assertion); test_every_fraction_and_percentage_is_bound_or_declared and test_every_statistical_quantity_is_bound_or_declared both match on numeric literals only; grep of the guard for 'sits above|sits below|inside the comparator' returns only the one regex literal and no comparison logic. | Artifact analyses.C_partner_prevalence.external_reported_share.falls_inside_pooled_interval is a stored true.

p1s.quote: §3.3: 'Agaram's arms differ about two-fold in mean follow-up (21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing *against* the TAF15 arm accruing events)' — §4.7: 'one whose arms differ roughly two-fold in mean follow-up (43.3 vs 21.7 months)'
p1s.why_wrong: The same pair is printed in OPPOSITE orders at the two sites, and neither site labels which arm is which. The only place the assignment exists is the artifact (TAF15 = 21.7, EWSR1 = 43.3). §3.3's parenthetical attaches a bias DIRECTION to an ordering the reader can only resolve by assuming first-mentioned = TAF15 — an assumption §4.7 immediately contradicts. A reader who carries §4.7's ordering back to §3.3 reads the direction backwards, and a future edit that harmonises the two orderings in the wrong direction silently inverts the paper's conservativeness argument. Both figures are numerically bound to the artifact by the guard, so the values are watched; the ARM LABEL is not, because it is never printed.
p1s.evidence: Artifact cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].strata['TAF15::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 21.7; strata['EWSR1::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 43.3. | Document lines: §3.3 '(21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing against the TAF15 arm accruing events)'; §4.7 '(43.3 vs 21.7 months)'. Neither sentence names an arm beside a number.

p2s.quote: This pooling therefore does not correct that figure: it replaces a point estimate with an interval over four independent series, and locates within it the cohort whose share is highest.
p2s.why_wrong: Read the natural way — 'locates X within it', X = the highest-share cohort, it = the interval — the sentence asserts that 29.2 % lies inside 12.9–25.0. It does not, and the Abstract and §5 say the opposite ('sits below the 29.2 %'). The intended reading is presumably 'identifies, among the four series, the one with the highest share', which the next sentence supplies. As written the clause contradicts the paper's own headline in the same paragraph.
p2s.evidence: Artifact analyses.C_partner_prevalence.pooled['TAF15::NR4A3'] ci95 = 12.9–25.0; heterogeneity_TAF15.range_percent = [15.8, 29.2]. Abstract: 'sits below the 29.2 % of the single referral-centre series that is the high outlier of the four.'

p2s.where: §2.4, §3.1 table, §3.3 table — every pooled Fisher p
p2s.quote: Fisher exact two-sided p-values are reported for each contrast. They are **post-hoc and descriptive only**
p2s.why_wrong: Each pooled p is computed on a MERGED 2x2 table with cohort collapsed away, not on a cohort-stratified table. For the secondary TKI pool that merge is across cohorts whose comparator rates are 21.1 % and 75.0 % (spread 53.9 points), so p = 0.155 is not a test of a common effect in any sense; for the death row (both cohorts pointing the same way) the merge is benign but still unstratified. An exact conditional / CMH test on the 2x2xK table is the matching instrument and is neither computed nor named. Graded P2 because §2.4 and §4.8 declare the p-values post-hoc and licensing nothing, and §4.8 explicitly describes p = 0.0034 as 'a post-hoc description of a 7-versus-6-event table across two cohorts' — which concedes the point without naming the stratification issue.
p2s.evidence: Recomputed exactly from artifact integers: Fisher two-sided on merged tables gives 0.15496 (0/5 vs 10/27), 1.0 (0/3 vs 4/19), 0.0033866 (7/15 vs 6/58), 0.73891 (4/15 vs 13/58), 0.51633 (5/15 vs 14/58) — reproducing every printed value, which confirms the merged-table construction. | Artifact analyses.A.secondary_assume_independent.heterogeneity.spread_percent = 53.9.

p2s.quote: Pooled, the gap is 9.2 points with overlapping intervals and post-hoc p = 0.5163.
p2s.why_wrong: Overlap of the two arms' confidence intervals is invoked as evidence of no difference. Arm-interval overlap is not a valid test in either direction — two intervals can overlap while the difference is significant — and here it does the work of the difference interval the paper never prints (STAT-P1-2). The error runs in the paper's conservative direction (it argues nothing is established), and the accompanying p = 0.5163 independently supports the conclusion, so this is P2 rather than higher. Same construction reappears in §5's metastasis bullet, where it is one of three grounds offered.
p2s.evidence: Artifact analyses.B_outcome_by_partner.distant_metastasis_after_presentation: taf15 33.3 (15.2–58.3), comparator 24.1 (15.0–36.5), fisher 0.5163. Intervals do overlap; the overlap carries no inferential content on its own.

p2s.where: Abstract, §3.5, §5 claims bullet — the prevalence comparison
p2s.quote: an interval that **contains** the ≈20 % this document's own cited sources state and sits below the 29.2 % of the single referral-centre series that is the high outlier of the four
p2s.why_wrong: The comparator 29.2 % is Agaram 2014's rate, and Agaram contributes 24 of the pooled 154 denominators and 7 of the 28 TAF15 events. The pooled interval and the figure it is said to sit below are therefore DEPENDENT quantities, and the interval is a homogeneity-assuming Wilson interval over cohorts whose rates span 13.4 points (STAT-P1-1). 'Sits below' is arithmetically true and the paper immediately supplies the correct framing (high outlier, referral-centre selection), so this is P2 — but as a comparison it establishes heterogeneity, not that the referral figure is high relative to an independent estimate.
p2s.evidence: Artifact analyses.C_partner_prevalence.cohorts_pooled includes agaram-2014-prevalence; partner_assigned_per_cohort['agaram-2014-prevalence'] = 24; heterogeneity_TAF15.per_cohort_percent['agaram-2014-prevalence'] = 29.2; pooled TAF15 ci95 12.9–25.0.

p2s.quote: but §4.3's conservative-floor reading applies to the outcome pool **on assumption rather than on measurement**: older outcome data most likely understate the outlook of a patient diagnosed today
p2s.why_wrong: §4.3's floor is a different claim about a different quantity: that partner-unassigned residues excluded from numerator and denominator make the pooled TAF15 PREVALENCE of 18.2 % an underestimate. It says nothing about era, outcome or the outcome pool. §4.11 (and Appendix A21) treat it as the source of an era-based conservative reading of the outcome figures. The substantive statement in §4.11 is correctly labelled an assumption, so the defect is the cross-reference rather than the claim.
p2s.evidence: Document §4.3: 'If variant partners are systematically harder to type … the pooled TAF15 share of 18.2 % is an **underestimate**' — the only floor argument in §4.3, and it is about prevalence. Document §4.11 and Appendix A21 both attribute an outcome/era floor to §4.3.

p2s.where: Abstract and §3.3 — an exhaustiveness superlative not in §2.3a's enumerated list
p2s.quote: **This is the first magnitude the prognostic contrast has ever had**
p2s.why_wrong: 'The first … ever' is a superlative taken over the literature, and §2.3a exists because no systematic search was run. §2.3a's generic clause ('equally every count and every superlative taken over the literature') does cover it, but its ENUMERATION — §3.3's 'Two cohorts publish…', §5's 'the only two cohorts…', 'the largest series to test metastasis by partner directly' — omits this one, and the enumeration is what a reader treats as the list of bounded statements. The claim is also the Abstract's, where §2.3a is 140 lines away — the same shape Appendix A16 corrected for the response claim by putting the bound in place. A related, smaller instance: 'the largest series to test metastasis by partner *directly*' excludes Paioli 2021 (n = 67, larger than Huang's 58), which also tests metastasis by partner but as a time-to-event endpoint; the distinction is stated one sentence later, but only 'directly' carries it in the superlative itself.
p2s.evidence: Document §2.3a enumerated list; Abstract and §3.3 carry 'the first magnitude this contrast has ever had' with no bound in place. | §3.3: 'the largest series to test metastasis by partner *directly* reports **P = .728**' against §3.4's Paioli 2021 n = 67 (DMFS p = 0.09), artifact cohorts[paioli-2021-outcome].n_assessable = 67 vs cohorts[huang-2023-outcome].n_assessable = 58.

what_you_could_not_break: Every Fisher exact two-sided p reproduces to the printed precision: 1.0, 0.155, 0.0034, 0.7389, 0.5163 (and the single-cohort 0.0672, 0.0264 retained in the artifact).

The denominator convention is consistent across all three analyses and every roster reconciles: Agaram 26 = 24 partner-assigned (16 EWSR1 + 7 TAF15 + 1 TCF12) + 2 unassigned, outcome arms 16 + 7 = 23 with follow-up; Huang 57 partner-assigned (46 + 9 + 2 TCF12), outcome arms 42 + 8 = 50 of the 53 with follow-up; pooled outcome 15 + 58 = 73; prevalence 120 + 28 + 5 + 1 = 154 over 24 + 57 + 11 + 62. Huang's metastasis partition adds correctly (at presentation + after = any: 8+8=16, 1+3=4). The 3+19 = 22 evaluable of the pazopanib trial matches the reported trial size.

The zero-event arms are handled correctly and the choice of estimator is pre-committed rather than selected after seeing the counts: §2.2's stated reason (the normal approximation degenerates at 0/n) is the right reason, and Wilson is what the artifact computes.

The TKI comparison is stated at its true weight and is the right comparison for the claim made: the upper bound is used only to show the data CANNOT EXCLUDE equality, never to claim a difference, and the paper says so explicitly ('The honest statement is a direction, not a difference'). Both pairings hold (56.1 > 21.1; 43.4 > 37.0).

The local-recurrence row IS correctly identified as a cancellation of two disagreeing cohorts rather than a small shared effect, with the comparator-arm spread (22.4 points) printed in the prose; the metastasis row's direction flip is likewise disclosed with both cohorts' rates. Per-cohort heterogeneity blocks exist in the artifact for every pooled figure (both arms of all three outcome rows, the secondary TKI pool, and prevalence).

The post-hoc status of every p-value is declared at §2.4, restated at §4.8 pointing at the correct current headline (0.0034), and the multiplicity across endpoints is disclosed as uncorrected. The authors' own three-way p-values are kept separate from this paper's two-way ones in the artifact with an explicit do-not-conflate note.

The adjustment claim, everywhere except §3.8 (STAT-B1), is stated correctly: one multivariable model (Huang), Paioli's structure recorded as UNKNOWN and explicitly not counted as a second, and the crude/adjusted distinction repeated at §3.3, §4.1a and §5 with the 'never quoted alone' instruction.

The prevalence pool's independence claim survives checking: the four cited author lists (5, 20, 18, 16 names, held unabridged in the artifact's citations records) intersect in nobody on surname-plus-initials or surname alone, matching the counts §3.5 prints.

The sensitivity analysis on the one unevaluable pazopanib patient is arithmetically right (0/2 and 4/20, upper bound 65.8 %) and correctly described as weakening the contrast, with no claim depending on it.

Confounders beyond size are named rather than suppressed: §4.1a lists Huang's five univariate factors and states the partner may be standing in for grade or chemotherapy allocation as readily as for size, and §4.9 states the referral/publication bias direction correctly (both inflate the apparent contrast).
could_not_check: Whether Agaram 2014's per-arm mean follow-up figures are means over all patients or over survivors only — the distinction determines how much of STAT-B3's circularity is present, but the source is not readable from this sandbox and the artifact records only the two scalars. The observation that would settle it: the follow-up definition in Agaram 2014's Clinical Follow-up section (PMC4015728, in the repository literature cache).

Whether Huang 2023's 5 patients without follow-up are distributed by partner — if they are TAF15-enriched, the 8-patient TAF15 outcome denominator is selected. The artifact records only that 53 of 58 had follow-up and that 3 of the 53 are the miscellaneous group. Settled by Table 1 of the published PDF.

Whether Paioli 2021's partner analysis was multivariable. The paper is right to record this as UNKNOWN (§3.4); I could not improve on that from the record held here, and STAT-B1 is a defect precisely because §3.8 does not.

The exact Fisher implementation in the generator (research/manuscripts/emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py) — I reproduced every printed p with a standard two-sided exact test on the hypergeometric point-probability criterion and all five matched, but I did not execute the generator, so an implementation difference that happens to agree on these five tables would not have been detected.
